summary: A weekly one-to-one between sales manager Chris Klevan and closer Ben Byrne. Ben opens by debriefing two calls he took that morning - one prospect who asked for a trial and left before objections could be handled, and one he judged to have no real gap - then raises his core problem, that his discovery stays at surface level and never reaches identity level. Chris coaches him to go straight to the why-now, to ask follow-up questions rather than gather data, and to soften the framing for prideful prospects who will not admit anything is going badly. The second half becomes a wide-ranging discussion of sales philosophy and trainers, including Eli Wilde, Chase Hughes, Josh and Brian, covering consciousness-level mapping of prospects, covert hypnotic technique, and elicitation. Chris books two additional weekly one-to-ones and asks Ben to bring a call to review to every meeting. Andrew Musial is waiting to be seen next.
notable: Ben Byrne describes elicitation as a technique he uses, and demonstrates it with a worked example of extracting a prospect's true hourly wage by asserting a figure he knew to be wrong: 'it's like getting information out of people without asking questions'. Chris responds 'That's a cool example' and 'like the spy people do it'.

Ben recounts Eli Wilde teaching a covert technique to bypass conscious awareness - 'you get the person to think about something exterior, then internal, then this, and the next thing you know, their conscious mind just drops, and then you can do this' - and adds 'why aren't we recording this right now?'

Chris maps prospects to consciousness levels (shame, fear, pride, reason, courage, acceptance) and selects tactics accordingly, including 'if they're a very prideful person, it can work great... you can kind of use it against them'.

Ben prejudges a prospect's ability to pay by US state - 'he's in Georgia, which is like, not to put limiting beliefs out there, but, you know, they don't make like a ton of money there' - and Chris endorses it: 'it's not a limiting belief if it's, like, rooted in reality'.

Chris describes his own core skill as 'I can break people down very, very fast', and says of a hypothetical prospect disclosing suicidality: 'I'd be like, oh, dude, tell me about it. I'm so sorry to hear that. I wouldn't skip a beat.'
Ben references a 'love it or leave it' option he mentioned to a prospect who asked for a trial. No guarantee of any kind was stated on any of the seven sales calls in this batch.
Chris states the sales process document was 'built off of the people here who were closing at 30-35%', establishing an internal close-rate benchmark.
Chris says of the pitch: 'I think the pitch is far less of a big deal than most people think it is. Because I think that people make the decision to buy before they ever even get to the pitch.'

Ben's self-diagnosis is that he is not yet reaching identity level; Chris's counter-diagnosis is confidence rather than technique - 'it's not like you're not asking good questions in a lot of cases. It's more like you just don't seem confident in what you're asking.'

Daniel, a candidate closer, had spoken to Chris earlier the same day and there is no headcount for him: 'I like him. I just don't have any space for him right now.' Ben notes 'I think he said he quit moves either today or yesterday' from a role where he had been 'top three for quite a few months'.

Ben's background is disclosed across the call: previously sold for Eli Wilde and for 'Boris', came out of 'closers', and is currently going through 'Josh's training' at another organisation whose Wednesday and Friday sessions run four hours.
Ben reports completing a three-day fast and Chris reports ongoing eczema he is seeing a dermatologist and allergist about, possibly linked to mould in his office.
